reason: French 'lobe stigmatique' is the lobe of a stigma.
Plural of R2401.
Basal nerves are the veins that leave the base of a leaf blade (palmate or plinerved leaves).
Plural of R2403.
French plural of R2403; 'nervure' is a vein.

A hair-point is a slender, often hyaline tip on an apex. It is not the apex itself. It also occurs on bracts, glumes and sepals. The existing value term hair-pointed (FLOPO:0991249) already covers the meaning. Keep it as a word-to-quality rule or reject it.
Plural of R2406. The hair-like tip is lost, and the part may not be a leaf.
Same as R2406. A hair point is a tip, not the apex.
'Hyaline' is a quality and the hair-point is only a tip of the apex. Same problem as R2406.
Limb of a leaf is the blade; 'leaf blade' is a synonym of leaf lamina.
Same as R2410.
Plural of peristome tooth.
Primary rays of an umbel are the first branches of the main axis. PO lists 'primary inflorescence branch' as a synonym of second order inflorescence axis.
Plural of R2413.
French form of R2413.
A male spike is a staminate inflorescence. The spike shape is lost, but the class is right.
A staminate spike is a staminate inflorescence.

'Serration' mostly names the state of the margin (serrate, a quality), not the tooth. It is a tooth only in counts or sizes such as 'serrations 3 per cm'. A word-only rule would turn margin descriptions into tooth statements.
Same as R2418. 'Crenation' names the crenate state of the margin more often than a tooth.
'Stock' usually means a rootstock or caudex-like base. It can also be the grafting stock or the garden plant Matthiola. Calling it stem loses the meaning. It is better rejected.
PO lists 'male inflorescence' as a synonym of staminate inflorescence.
Plural of colleter.
Colleter is right, but the rule loses that the colleter is on the calyx. Add the calyx (PO_0009060) as container_id.
A pseudopedicel is a stalk-like part that is not a true pedicel, so the generic stalk is acceptable.
A bract on the peduncle of an inflorescence is an inflorescence bract.
A pseudopanicle is an inflorescence. The specific form has no PO class, so the generic class is the safe choice.
A cymose panicle is an inflorescence. The generic class is safe.
'Phyllaryphyll' is not a botanical word. It looks like a broken form of 'phyllary', which is a synonym of involucral bract. Fix the text normalisation instead of adding a rule.
A corm tunic is the tunic of a corm. The rule loses the corm but the class is right.
Plural of R2429.
'Outer' is a position word. The part is the tunic.
In a fused corolla the lobe is not a separate petal, so petal margin is wrong. The bearer is the corolla lobe (FLOPO_0986006).
Same as R2432. The part is the corolla lobe, not the petal.
French form of R2432. The part is the corolla lobe.
'With domatia' is a statement that the part is present, not a part name. It needs an entity_presence rule for domatium. A bearer rule would treat 'with domatia' as the bearer.
Same as R2435. 'Avec domaties' states presence and needs an entity_presence rule.
Leaf hair is a leaf trichome.
Plural of R2437.
French form of R2437.
Integument is the ovule integument only when the part is an ovule. In seed descriptions it may mean the seed coat.
Plural of R2440.
French 'tégument' is mostly the seed coat or seed integument. It is the ovule integument only for an ovule. Use a constraint on ovule, or reject the rule.
A tetrad in pollen descriptions is a tetrad of microspores.
A pollen tetrad is a tetrad of microspores.
A pseudo-umbel is an umbel-like inflorescence whose branching is not always cymose. Cyme inflorescence is too specific, so use the generic inflorescence.
Same as R2445.
French form of R2445.
A sterile stamen is a staminode.
A culm sheath is the sheath of a (culm) leaf. It is acceptable, but bamboo culm sheaths are a special organ.
The perigone is the perianth, so the perigone tube is the perianth tube.
